note: Maps every distinct Curation/DataSource value in BindingDB 202610 to a class.
Authored AFTER the ingest census, because the census is what establishes that
the set of values is small and closed: exactly 9 values across 3,243,660 rows.
An unmapped value encountered later is a hard error, not an 'other' default --
a new release introducing a source must be classified deliberately, since the
class drives IC50 tiering and metadata confidence.
This file is hashed into the curation profile, so a change to it invalidates
the artifacts produced under the previous mapping.

literature_curated.description: Measurements curated from a primary publication, with the assay described upstream even though BindingDB does not carry that description.
values: Curated from the literature by BindingDB

patent.description: Measurements transcribed from a patent examples table. Provenance is real and citable, but a patent record cannot evidence which biochemical assay produced a value, and one patent's table may span more than one protocol.

pubchem_bioassay.description: Imported from a PubChem BioAssay deposition. Often high-throughput screening output, where a single reported potency may come from a concentration series of very few points.

screening_panel.description: A dedicated assay programme running one consistent protocol across many ligands. PDSP is radioligand binding and reports Ki only; it contributes no IC50, so IC50 tiering never applies to it.

structure_challenge.description: Community structure-prediction and affinity-prediction challenge sets. Small, and their provenance is the challenge rather than a primary assay record.

other.description: Single-laboratory direct depositions that fit no class above.

ic50_tier_a_rationale: The specification admits IC50 to the primary regression only when the record
supports assignment to the intended protein and an appropriate biochemical
assay. literature_curated and patent records carry a citable primary source;
pubchem_bioassay, structure_challenge and other do not establish a biochemical
assay for the intended protein and go to the flagged tier.
Tiering is keyed on this class, NEVER on PubChem AID presence. Measured: 68% of
rows carry an AID, including ~545k whose provenance is a US patent, so an
AID-based rule would misclassify most of the patent corpus.
metadata_confidence_rationale: A patent is capped at medium however complete its other fields are, because a
single patent examples table can hold thousands of IC50 values under more than
one protocol, so citation identity is a weaker proxy for assay identity there
than it is for a primary paper.
Measured caveat worth carrying into the report: pooled within-publication
replicate SD is LOWER for patents than for literature (Kd 0.707 vs 1.019
p-units). That indicates re-statement of one table value rather than
independent measurement -- less independence, not better precision.
